title: Kaggle CLI — Configuration essentials
description: Kaggle CLI is configured through a small, explicit surface: `kaggle.token`, `kaggle.unzip`, `kaggle.quiet`. The demo below validates a sample configuration against the required keys, because most Kaggle CLI failures are configuration mistakes, and a validator catches them before they cost time.

kaggle kernels push uploads a notebook as a Kaggle Kernel.
The -p flag unzips downloads into a target folder.
demo_code:
required = ['kaggle.token', 'kaggle.unzip', 'kaggle.quiet']
sample = {
    'kaggle.token': '~/.kaggle/kaggle.json',
    'kaggle.unzip': True,
    'kaggle.quiet': False,
}
print('CONFIG VALIDATION')
ok = True
for k in required:
    good = k in sample and sample[k] not in (None, '')
    ok = ok and good
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'}] {k} = {sample.get(k)!r}")
print('RESULT:', 'valid configuration' if ok else 'INVALID')

  [PASS] kaggle.unzip = True

title: Kaggle CLI — Data formats and portability
description: Portability is a feature: Kaggle CLI works with kaggle.json token, Dataset zips/CSVs, Kernel metadata. The demo below proves the round-trip — serialize a sample record, parse it back, verify byte-for-byte equality — because data you cannot move is data you do not own.
facts: kaggle datasets download -d owner/slug fetches a dataset as a zip.
kaggle datasets list -s 'query' searches the library from the terminal.
kaggle competitions download -c <name> pulls challenge data after accepting rules.
demo_code:
import json
record = {'tool': 'Kaggle CLI', 'format': 'kaggle.json token', 'n': 1}
blob = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)
back = json.loads(blob)
assert back == record, 'round-trip mismatch'
print('serialize  :', blob)
print('round-trip : OK (byte-identical)')
print('formats archived: ' + 'kaggle.json token, Dataset zips/CSVs, Kernel metadata')
